content: We need to determine number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of the molecule. We can use IR spectra to detect carbonyl stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-210 ppm). The cheapest is IR? The IR tool returns spectra string; we can look for C=O stretch around 1700 cm-1. That would indicate number of carbonyl groups? Might be ambiguous if overlapping. Could also use carbon NMR to see carbonyl peaks. Probably IR is cheaper. Use ir_spectra tool.
